newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Police teargas stock traders in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Police teargas stock traders in Bangladesh.

text.p: Police fired teargas and used batons to subdue violent punters protesting the fall of share prices on Dhaka's kerb market on Wednesday, forcing brokers to lock themselves in their chambers, police said.
Police went into action outside the exchange building after hundreds of kerb market traders assaulted a broker and attacked a fellow seller who was offloading shares at lower prices.
"It turned into a battleground with panicked investors running for cover. We needed to act to restore order," one police officer said.
Broker Mahbub Morshed, speaking during the fighting that lasted around three hours, said: "We are not able to come out for fear of our lives. The streets may be unsafe."
Several people were injured in the melee, one witness told reporters. Police said they made no arrests.
The kerb market refers to trading that takes place outside official market hours. In Bangladesh, it always takes place outside the exchange building.

The battle raged on the streets after brokers from the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) threatened to seek legal action against the Securities and Exchange Commission, the stock market watchdog, for stopping company directors from becoming brokers.

The DSE all-share index dropped to 3,298.04 points at close of trading on Wednesday from 3,448.88 a week ago following the SEC move and statements by opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia that Bangladesh stock markets have been flooded by illegal funds from India.
DSE chairman Imtiyaz Husain expressed concern over the recent SEC steps and cautioned they might discourage investors.
"I am concerned about the happenings in the name of market regulations. We are not being heard..." he told Reuters on Wednesday.
SEC Chairman Harunur Rashid rejected the criticism.
"We certainly consulted the DSE before taking any action," Rashid told Reuters. "What we are doing is nothing other than for streamlining the stock market."
A meeting of DSE members on Tuesday night expressed their "anguish" over the SEC's recent regulatory moves, broker Mushtaque Ahmed told Reuters.
He said they were angry about the SEC directive that barred directors of companies listed on the stock exchange from remaining or becoming a broker.
The meeting was attended by 155 of the DSE's 195 members, who criticised the SEC for "imposing decisions unilaterally".
"We fell that this (SEC) move is to curb our fundamental rights. The government should speed up its decision to increase the supply of scrips in the market," Husain said.
"The government had created a panic in the share market in the name of enforcing regulations. It should not interfere with the affairs of the market."
